skill.name: using-agent-relay
skill.description: Coordinates registered Agent Relay participants through MCP tools for workspaces, messaging, channels, actions, and worker management.
skill.summary: Coordinate registered AI agents through Agent Relay workspaces, messages, channels, actions, and delegated workers.
skill.author: AgentWorkforce

security_audit.summary: All 77 external-command findings are false positives from Markdown backticks and fenced examples; the file contains no executable implementation. Four network findings are confirmed because agents are directed to hosted content or an external Relay gateway. Semantic review found unpinned remote instructions and credential examples that place secrets in command arguments.

remediation.issue: Agents are directed to mutable instructions hosted outside the audited skill.
remediation.suggestion: Include the role-selection instructions locally or reference a version-pinned artifact with verified integrity. Remove the remote instruction URL from spawned worker tasks.

remediation.issue: Workspace keys and agent tokens appear as command-line flags in examples.
remediation.suggestion: Use environment or session-based secret handling in every example. Warn users that command arguments can be exposed through history and process inspection.

remediation.issue: The examples configure an external Relay gateway.
remediation.suggestion: Document the endpoint owner, transmitted data, authentication expectations, and required user approval before connecting.

content.value_statement: Multi-agent work can lose context when participants use inconsistent tools and status formats. This skill standardizes Relay registration, messaging, coordination, and worker delegation.
actual_capabilities: Joins or creates an Agent Relay workspace and registers the current session.
Discovers agents and channels, joins channels, and checks unread activity.
Sends direct messages, group messages, channel posts, and thread replies.
Searches message history, marks messages read, and manages reactions.
Lists and invokes available Relay actions and submits configured task results.
Spawns and releases provider-backed workers when the participant role permits delegation.
limitations: Requires an Agent Relay MCP server or CLI and valid workspace access.
Targets registered participants, not outside orchestrators managing a local broker.
Action invocation and structured result submission depend on server configuration.
Remote handoff content is not pinned or verified by this skill.

use_cases.title: Join a Relay Assignment
use_cases.description: Register a spawned worker, inspect its inbox, acknowledge the lead, and begin the assigned scope.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Specialist Workers
use_cases.description: Send targeted updates, organize channel discussions, delegate permitted work, and collect completion evidence.

use_cases.title: Monitor Distributed Work
use_cases.description: Review messages, threads, readers, reactions, and worker status across an active workspace.

prompt_templates.title: Join and Acknowledge
prompt_templates.prompt: Join workspace <workspace-key>, register as <agent-name>, check the inbox, and acknowledge <lead-name> before starting <scope>.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a spawned participant

prompt_templates.title: Review Team Activity
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Relay inbox and channel activity. Summarize priorities, identify blockers, and send concise status updates to the correct recipients.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve a Shared Blocker
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Relay messages for <topic>, inspect relevant threads, contact affected agents, and post a channel summary with owners and next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Delegate and Close Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Confirm my role permits delegation. Spawn a <provider> worker for <task>, monitor progress, collect evidence, report completion, and release the worker.

output_examples.input: Join the provided workspace as api-worker and acknowledge the lead.
output_examples.output: Joined the workspace, registered as api-worker, checked the inbox, and sent the lead an acknowledgment for the assigned API scope.

output_examples.input: Find recent authentication blockers and update the team.
output_examples.output: Found two authentication discussions, summarized the active blocker, contacted its owner, and posted the agreed next step in the working channel.

output_examples.input: Delegate a focused review and close the worker after acceptance.
output_examples.output: Started a permitted review worker, tracked its response, shared the findings with the lead, and released the worker after acceptance.

best_practices: Confirm the workspace and registration state before calling participant-only tools.
Use direct messages for targeted coordination and channels for information relevant to the whole team.
Send acknowledgment, status, blocker, and completion updates with specific evidence.
anti_patterns: Do not use participant tools as a substitute for the outside orchestrator workflow.
Do not place real workspace keys or agent tokens in messages or command history.
Do not spawn workers unless the current role explicitly permits delegation.

faq.question: What must be configured before using this skill?
faq.answer: An Agent Relay MCP server or CLI must be available. You also need a workspace and a registered agent identity.

faq.question: Does this skill start the local Relay broker?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on registered participants. Use the separate orchestrator workflow to start brokers and manage workers from outside Relay.

faq.question: Can this skill create additional workers?
faq.answer: Yes, when the current role permits delegation and the Relay server exposes worker management tools.

faq.question: Which AI clients are supported?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: How should credentials be handled?
faq.answer: Keep workspace keys and agent tokens in secure session or environment storage. Do not post them in messages or shared logs.

faq.question: Does every Relay server expose the same tools?
faq.answer: No. Actions and structured result submission appear only when the server and spawned task enable them.
